# openCenter AirGap

> Build tool for creating air-gapped Kubernetes deployment packages. Collects container images, binaries, OS packages, and Python dependencies into a single cryptographically verifiable Zarf artifact for disconnected deployments.

## Operator Guidance

- Use `opencenter-build init` to create project structure with default versions.env
- Edit config/versions.env to pin all component versions (single source of truth)
- Run `opencenter-build build` to auto-generate components.yaml and create Zarf package
- Use `opencenter-build scan --repos` to auto-discover images and charts from repositories
- Verify packages with `opencenter-build verify --all` before transfer to air-gapped sites
- Deploy on bastion host with `zarf package deploy` to serve local registry and repos
- All builds are deterministic and cryptographically signed with Cosign

## Installation

### Prerequisites and Setup

Source: openCenter-AirGap/README.md

Install openCenter AirGap on a connected build host (Zone A) with Python 3.10+, Git, and 100GB+ free disk space.

```bash
# Clone repository
git clone <repo-url>
cd openCenter-AirGap

# Install package in development mode
pip install -e .

# Verify installation
opencenter-airgap --help
```

### Development Installation

Source: openCenter-AirGap/CONTRIBUTING.md

Install with development dependencies for contributing code, including pytest, black, mypy, and pre-commit hooks.

```bash
# Install with development dependencies
pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Install pre-commit hooks
pre-commit install

# Verify development environment
pytest tests/unit/ -v
black --check src/ tests/
mypy src/
```

## Quickstart

### Initialize and Build Package

Source: openCenter-AirGap/README.md

Create a new air-gap package by initializing the project, editing versions, and running the build command. The build auto-generates components.yaml from versions.env.

```bash
# 1. Initialize project (creates default versions.env)
opencenter-airgap init

# 2. Edit versions (single source of truth)
vim config/versions.env

# 3. Build (auto-generates components.yaml from versions.env)
opencenter-airgap build

# 4. Optional: Auto-discover images/charts from repos
opencenter-airgap scan --repos
```

### Deploy Package in Air-Gap

Source: openCenter-AirGap/README.md

Transfer the Zarf package to disconnected site (Zone C) and deploy on bastion host to serve local registry and package repositories.

```bash
# On bastion host (requires Zarf CLI)
zarf package deploy zarf-package-*.tar.zst --confirm

# Verify deployment
kubectl get nodes
kubectl get pods -A
```

## Core Concepts

### Three-Zone Air-Gap Model

Source: openCenter-AirGap/README.md

The deployment follows a three-zone security model: Zone A (Factory) downloads dependencies with internet access, Zone B (Airlock) handles physical media transfer, and Zone C (Field) deploys without internet connectivity.

```
Zone A: Factory (Connected)
  ├── Download from internet
  ├── Package into Zarf artifact
  └── Generate SBOM and sign

Zone B: Airlock (Physical Transfer)
  └── USB, DVD, or secure courier

Zone C: Field (Disconnected)
  ├── Bastion serves local registry (port 5000)
  ├── Bastion serves package repos (port 8080)
  └── Target nodes pull from bastion only
```

### Component Manifest Auto-Generation

Source: openCenter-AirGap/README.md

The build command automatically generates components.yaml from versions.env. If versions.env is updated, the next build regenerates the manifest while preserving manual additions.

```bash
# Initial build generates components.yaml
opencenter-airgap build

# Add custom components after initial build
opencenter-airgap add image custom-registry.io/app:v1.0
opencenter-airgap add tool --name mytool --version v1.0 --url <url>

# Rebuild preserves custom additions
opencenter-airgap build

# Force clean regeneration (loses manual edits)
opencenter-airgap build --force-regenerate
```

### Bastion Architecture

Source: openCenter-AirGap/README.md

A bastion is a single node in the target environment that runs local registry (port 5000) and package repositories (port 8080). Target nodes pull all dependencies from bastion instead of internet.

```bash
# Bastion services after deployment
curl http://localhost:5000/v2/_catalog  # Container registry
curl http://localhost:8080/debs/        # APT repository
```

## Common Recipes

### Add Container Images

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/cli-commands.md

Add container images to the manifest for inclusion in the air-gap package.

```bash
# Add single image
opencenter-build add image docker.io/library/nginx:1.25.0

# Add image with digest (recommended for production)
opencenter-build add image registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.34.3 \
  --digest sha256:abc123...
```

### Add Helm Charts

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/cli-commands.md

Add Helm charts from repositories to deploy applications in the air-gapped cluster.

```bash
# Add Helm chart
opencenter-build add chart ingress-nginx \
  --version 4.7.0 \
  --source https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx

# Add cert-manager chart
opencenter-build add chart cert-manager \
  --version v1.13.0 \
  --source https://charts.jetstack.io
```

### Add CLI Tools and Binaries

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/cli-commands.md

Add command-line tools and Kubernetes binaries to the package for operator use.

```bash
# Add kubectl binary
opencenter-build add tool \
  --name kubectl \
  --version v1.34.3 \
  --url https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.34.3/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl

# Add Helm CLI
opencenter-build add tool \
  --name helm \
  --version v3.14.0 \
  --url https://get.helm.sh/helm-v3.14.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz
```

### Scan Repositories for Components

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/cli-commands.md

Auto-discover container images and Helm charts from Git repositories like Kubespray and GitOps repos.

```bash
# Clone repos from versions.env and scan
opencenter-build scan --repos

# Scan specific directory
opencenter-build scan --repo build/kubespray

# Scan multiple directories
opencenter-build scan --repo build/kubespray --repo build/opencenter-gitops-base
```

### Resume Failed Build

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/cli-commands.md

Resume a build from the last checkpoint if it failed due to network issues or other transient errors.

```bash
# Resume from last checkpoint
opencenter-build build --resume

# Clean build (remove work directory first)
opencenter-build build --clean
```

### Verify Package Integrity

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/cli-commands.md

Verify package checksum, cryptographic signature, and SBOM before transferring to air-gapped site.

```bash
# Verify checksum
opencenter-build verify dist/zarf-package-*.tar.zst --checksum

# Verify signature (requires public key)
opencenter-build verify dist/zarf-package-*.tar.zst --signature

# Full verification (all checks)
opencenter-build verify dist/zarf-package-*.tar.zst --all
```

## Configuration

### Version Configuration (versions.env)

Source: openCenter-AirGap/config/versions.env

The versions.env file is the single source of truth for all component versions. Edit this file to pin Kubernetes, container runtime, and application versions.

```bash
# Kubernetes versions
KUBERNETES_VERSION="v1.34.3"
KUBESPRAY_VERSION="master"

# Container runtime
CONTAINERD_VERSION="2.1.5"
RUNC_VERSION="1.3.4"
CNI_VERSION="1.8.0"
CALICO_VERSION="v3.31.3"

# Core services
FLUXCD_VERSION="v2.7.5"
GITEA_VERSION="v1.25.4"
CERT_MANAGER_VERSION="v1.16.2"
INGRESS_NGINX_VERSION="v1.9.0"

# Operator tools
KUBECTL_VERSION="v1.34.3"
HELM_VERSION="v4.0.5"
K9S_VERSION="v0.50.9"

# Terraform
TERRAFORM_VERSION="1.14.0"
OPENSTACK_PROVIDER_VERSION="2.1.0"
```

### Component Manifest Schema

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/component-manifest-schema.md

The components.yaml manifest defines what gets packaged. It is auto-generated from versions.env but can be customized with manual additions.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: opencenter-airgap
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Air-gapped Kubernetes deployment package

components:
  # Container images
  - name: registry
    type: image
    image: docker.io/library/registry:2.8.3
    digest: sha256:a1b2c3d4e5f6...
    platform: linux/amd64

  # Helm charts
  - name: cert-manager
    type: chart
    repository: https://charts.jetstack.io
    chart: cert-manager
    version: v1.13.0
    values:
      installCRDs: true

  # Binaries
  - name: kubectl
    type: binary
    url: https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.34.3/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl
    checksum: sha256:abc123...
    destination: /usr/local/bin/kubectl
    mode: "0755"

  # Repositories
  - name: kubespray
    type: repository
    url: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubespray.git
    ref: v2.24.0
    destination: /opt/opencenter/kubespray
```

### Node Inventory Configuration

Source: openCenter-AirGap/examples/nodes-baremetal.yaml

Define cluster topology for Kubespray deployment with control plane and worker nodes.

```yaml
control_plane:
  - hostname: control-01
    ip: 192.168.1.10
  - hostname: control-02
    ip: 192.168.1.11
  - hostname: control-03
    ip: 192.168.1.12

workers:
  - hostname: worker-01
    ip: 192.168.1.20
  - hostname: worker-02
    ip: 192.168.1.21
  - hostname: worker-03
    ip: 192.168.1.22
```

### Zarf Package Variables

Source: openCenter-AirGap/zarf.yaml

Configure deployment variables for Zarf package including bastion IP, SSH user, and service ports.

```yaml
variables:
- name: DEPLOYMENT_MODE
  description: 'Deployment mode: baremetal or openstack'
  default: baremetal
  prompt: false

- name: BASTION_IP
  description: IP address of bastion host
  default: ""
  prompt: true

- name: SSH_USER
  description: SSH user for node access
  default: deployer
  prompt: false

- name: REGISTRY_PORT
  description: Local registry port
  default: '35000'
  prompt: false
```

## API Patterns

### Python CLI Module Usage

Source: openCenter-AirGap/src/opencenter_build/cli.py

Import and use openCenter build modules programmatically for custom build workflows.

```python
from opencenter_build.config import load_versions_env, BuildConfig
from opencenter_build.validation import ConfigValidator
from pathlib import Path

# Load version configuration
versions = load_versions_env(Path("config/versions.env"))

# Create build configuration
config = BuildConfig(
    config_file=Path("config/versions.env"),
    output_dir=Path("dist"),
    work_dir=Path("build"),
    parallel_workers=4
)

# Validate configuration
validator = ConfigValidator(Path("config/schemas"))
validator.validate_versions_env(versions)
```

### Image Reference Parsing

Source: openCenter-AirGap/src/opencenter_build/image_utils.py

Parse and normalize container image references for registry operations.

```python
from opencenter_build.image_utils import parse_image_reference, normalize_image_reference

# Parse image reference
ref = parse_image_reference("docker.io/library/nginx:1.25.0")
print(ref.registry)    # docker.io
print(ref.repository)  # library/nginx
print(ref.tag)         # 1.25.0

# Normalize image reference
normalized = normalize_image_reference("nginx:1.25.0")
print(normalized)  # docker.io/library/nginx:1.25.0
```

### Build State Management

Source: openCenter-AirGap/src/opencenter_build/state.py

Manage build state with atomic operations and checkpoint/resume support.

```python
from opencenter_build.state import StateManager
from pathlib import Path

# Initialize state manager
state_mgr = StateManager(Path("build/state.json"))

# Write state atomically
state_mgr.write({
    "phase": "ASSET_COLLECTION",
    "progress": {"images": 45, "total": 120}
})

# Read current state
state = state_mgr.read()
print(state["phase"])  # ASSET_COLLECTION
```

### Logging Configuration

Source: openCenter-AirGap/src/opencenter_build/logging.py

Configure structured logging with JSON output and trace IDs for build operations.

```python
from opencenter_build.logging import setup_logging, get_logger, set_trace_id
import logging

# Setup logging
setup_logging(
    level=logging.INFO,
    log_file="build.log",
    json_output=True
)

# Get logger
logger = get_logger(__name__)

# Set trace ID for request tracking
trace_id = set_trace_id()
logger.info("Starting build", extra={"trace_id": trace_id})
```

## Troubleshooting

### Connection Timeout During Download

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/troubleshooting.md

Network timeouts during asset download can be caused by firewall rules or proxy configuration.

```bash
# Check connectivity
curl -I https://registry.k8s.io
curl -I https://github.com

# Configure proxy if needed
export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.example.com:8080
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.example.com:8080
opencenter-build build
```

### Disk Space Exhausted

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/troubleshooting.md

Build requires 100GB+ disk space. Clean previous builds or use external volume.

```bash
# Check disk usage
df -h build/ dist/
du -sh build/* | sort -h

# Clean previous builds
opencenter-build build --clean

# Use external volume
opencenter-build build \
  --work-dir /mnt/large-disk/build \
  --output-dir /mnt/large-disk/dist
```

### Registry Fails to Start on Bastion

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/troubleshooting.md

Registry container may fail if port 5000 is in use or insufficient disk space.

```bash
# Check registry logs
podman logs registry

# Check port availability
lsof -i :5000

# Check disk space
df -h /opt/opencenter

# Fix permissions
sudo chown -R $(whoami):$(whoami) /opt/opencenter/images
```

### Pods Stuck in ImagePullBackOff

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/troubleshooting.md

Nodes may fail to pull images if containerd is not configured to use bastion registry.

```bash
# Check containerd config on node
ssh node1 "cat /etc/containerd/config.toml | grep registry"

# Expected configuration
[plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".registry.mirrors."docker.io"]
  endpoint = ["http://BASTION_IP:5000"]

# Verify registry is reachable
ssh node1 "curl http://BASTION_IP:5000/v2/_catalog"

# Restart containerd
ssh node1 "sudo systemctl restart containerd"
```

### Ansible Fails with Unreachable Host

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/troubleshooting.md

SSH connectivity issues can prevent Ansible from reaching target nodes.

```bash
# Test SSH manually
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa user@node1

# Add SSH key to agent
eval $(ssh-agent)
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa

# Disable host key checking (first run only)
export ANSIBLE_HOST_KEY_CHECKING=False
ansible-playbook -i inventory.yml cluster.yml
```

### Resume Failed Build

Source: openCenter-AirGap/docs/reference/troubleshooting.md

Resume build from last checkpoint if it failed due to transient errors.

```bash
# Resume from last checkpoint
opencenter-build build --resume

# Check build status
opencenter-build status

# Delete state to start fresh
rm build/state.json
opencenter-build build
```

## Security Notes

### Cryptographic Signing and Verification

Source: openCenter-AirGap/SECURITY.md

All packages are cryptographically signed with Cosign for authenticity verification before deployment.

```bash
# Sign package (build host)
cosign sign --key ~/.opencenter/cosign.key zarf-package-*.tar.zst

# Verify signature (air-gap site)
cosign verify --key ~/.opencenter/cosign.pub zarf-package-*.tar.zst

# Verify with opencenter-build
opencenter-build verify dist/zarf-package-*.tar.zst --signature
```

### Secrets Management

Source: openCenter-AirGap/SECURITY.md

Secrets are managed via file-based injection with strict permissions, never committed to git.

```bash
# Create secrets directory
mkdir -p .secrets
chmod 700 .secrets

# Add secret file
echo "ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxx" > .secrets/github-token
chmod 600 .secrets/github-token

# Use in code
from opencenter_build.secrets import SecretsManager
secrets = SecretsManager(Path(".secrets"))
token = secrets.get_secret("github-token")
```

### Image Vulnerability Scanning

Source: openCenter-AirGap/SECURITY.md

Trivy scans all container images for HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs during build phase.

```bash
# Scan images during build (automatic)
opencenter-build build

# View scan results
cat build/image-scan-results.json | jq '.[] | select(.severity == "CRITICAL")'

# Build fails on CRITICAL CVEs by default
# Override with --skip-scanning (not recommended)
```

### SBOM Generation

Source: openCenter-AirGap/SECURITY.md

Complete software bill of materials (SBOM) is generated for every build and included in Zarf package.

```bash
# SBOM generated automatically during build
opencenter-build build

# View SBOM
jq '.artifacts[] | select(.name == "kubectl")' dist/zarf-package-*-sbom.json

# Verify SBOM
opencenter-build verify dist/zarf-package-*.tar.zst --sbom
```

### Dependency Pinning

Source: openCenter-AirGap/SECURITY.md

All versions are locked to commit SHAs in versions.env for supply chain security.

```bash
# Pin specific commit SHA
KUBESPRAY_COMMIT_SHA="a1b2c3d4e5f6..."
OPENCENTER_GITOPS_BASE_COMMIT_SHA="f6e5d4c3b2a1..."

# Verify checksums
cat build/asset-checksums.json | jq '.[] | select(.name == "kubectl")'
```

## Examples

### Complete Build Workflow

Source: openCenter-AirGap/README.md

End-to-end workflow from initialization to package creation with version pinning and verification.

```bash
# 1. Initialize project
opencenter-build init my-airgap-project
cd my-airgap-project

# 2. Edit versions
cat > config/versions.env << EOF
KUBERNETES_VERSION="v1.34.3"
CONTAINERD_VERSION="2.1.5"
FLUXCD_VERSION="v2.7.5"
CERT_MANAGER_VERSION="v1.16.2"
EOF

# 3. Build package
opencenter-build build

# 4. Verify package
opencenter-build verify dist/zarf-package-*.tar.zst --all

# 5. Check build status
opencenter-build status
```

### Custom Component Addition

Source: openCenter-AirGap/examples/components.yaml

Add custom images, charts, and tools to the auto-generated manifest.

```bash
# Add custom application image
opencenter-build add image ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:v1.2.3

# Add custom Helm chart
opencenter-build add chart myapp \
  --version 1.2.3 \
  --source https://charts.myorg.com

# Add custom CLI tool
opencenter-build add tool \
  --name myctl \
  --version v1.0.0 \
  --url https://releases.myorg.com/myctl-v1.0.0-linux-amd64

# Rebuild with custom additions
opencenter-build build
```

### OpenStack Deployment

Source: openCenter-AirGap/examples/openstack-config.yaml

Initialize project with OpenStack template for VM-based deployments with Terraform.

```bash
# Initialize with OpenStack template
opencenter-build init --template openstack

# Edit OpenStack configuration
vim config/openstack-config.yaml

# Build includes Terraform providers
opencenter-build build

# Deploy to OpenStack
cd /opt/opencenter/terraform
terraform init
terraform apply
```

### Development Testing

Source: openCenter-AirGap/CONTRIBUTING.md

Run tests with coverage reporting and type checking for development contributions.

```bash
# Run unit tests
pytest tests/unit/ -v

# Run with coverage
pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html

# Type checking
mypy src/

# Linting
pylint src/
black --check src/ tests/

# Run all checks
make test lint
```

### Multi-Site Deployment

Source: openCenter-AirGap/README.md

Build once and deploy identical packages to multiple edge sites for consistency.

```bash
# Build package once
opencenter-build build
sha256sum dist/zarf-package-*.tar.zst > package.sha256

# Copy to multiple sites
for site in site1 site2 site3; do
  scp dist/zarf-package-*.tar.zst $site:/tmp/
  scp package.sha256 $site:/tmp/
done

# Deploy at each site
ssh site1 "cd /tmp && sha256sum -c package.sha256 && zarf package deploy zarf-package-*.tar.zst --confirm"
```
